questions.question: Do you see the 'no data' message confirming the data was cleared?
questions.why: The screen displays 'no data' below the buttons, which confirms that the history was successfully cleared.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the peace of mind that comes from visually confirming their privacy action actually took effect.
questions.check: Does the page now display a 'no data' or empty-state message where the history was?
questions.say_example: The page now says <no data>. The history is gone.

questions.question: Does the dialog confirm that your selected data has been cleared?
questions.why: The dialog explicitly states that the selected data has been removed from Chrome and your synced devices, verifying that your privacy change was successful.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the reassurance of reading the success confirmation and the important reminder about other forms of history still stored in your Google account.
questions.check: Does the dialog state that the selected data has been removed, and from where (this device, synced devices)?
questions.say_example: The page confirms it: the data you picked is cleared, here and on your synced devices.

questions.question: Are all the security checkmarks complete?
questions.why: The screen displays a green shield and checkmarks next to each security item, confirming the account is protected.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the direct visual reassurance of seeing the green checkmarks that confirm their account's security status.
questions.check: Does each checkup item show a completed checkmark, and does the summary show the protected state?
questions.say_example: Every item on the checkup shows a green check. Nothing left flagged.

questions.question: Did a brief confirmation toast, such as 'Settings updated', appear and vanish at the bottom of the screen?
questions.why: Many apps confirm privacy changes with a temporary toast notification rather than a persistent state change or dialog box.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the immediate, definitive proof of success if the agent fails to read the screen during the brief window the message is visible.
questions.check: Did a confirmation toast (e.g. 'Settings updated') appear after the change?
questions.say_example: A little note flashed at the bottom - <Settings updated>. That's the page's way of confirming it saved.

questions.question: Should you review third-party app access before tapping OK?
questions.why: The dialog warns that installed third-party apps might still access your account unless you explicitly revoke their permissions.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the certainty that your account is fully secure from third-party apps that might still retain access on the device.
questions.check: Does the dialog warn that third-party apps may still have access unless their permissions are revoked separately?
questions.say_example: One warning before OK: apps you connected before can still reach the account until their access is removed. That's a separate list - I'll look at it and report what's there.

questions.question: Is there local browsing history remaining after deleting my Google account activity?
questions.why: The screen showed a list of visited sites, indicating that local browser history was not removed by the account-level deletion.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that their local device history is fully cleared alongside their account activity.
questions.check: Does the browser's own history page still list visited sites after the account-level deletion?
questions.say_example: Your <Google> account activity is deleted, but this phone still keeps its own browsing history. That needs its own clearing step - it's in the report.

questions.question: Do you see any of your past searches in the address bar dropdown?
questions.why: The dropdown showed 'Trending searches' and generic queries instead of personal history, confirming the setting change took effect.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the direct visual confirmation that their personal search history has been successfully removed from the search bar's autocomplete suggestions.
questions.check: Does the address bar dropdown show personal past searches, or only generic/trending suggestions?
questions.say_example: Typed in the address bar to test. Only <trending searches> come up, none of your own. It's really gone.

questions.question: Is the profile locked from public view?
questions.why: The screen shows 'No posts available' from the public perspective, confirming the privacy change took effect.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the peace of mind of personally verifying that their private information is no longer publicly visible.
questions.check: Does the profile viewed from outside show a locked/empty state (e.g. 'No posts available')?
questions.say_example: Looked at your profile from the outside. It shows <no posts available>. Locked, like you wanted.

questions.question: Do the before and after profile views confirm the 'Private account' badge was removed?
questions.why: Verifying that the lock icon and 'Private account' text disappeared from the main profile ensures the setting change actually took effect.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the direct visual confirmation that your profile's public visibility status successfully updated.
questions.check: Does the profile still show the 'Private account' label and lock, or are they gone?
questions.say_example: From the outside, the <Private account> label and lock are gone. You're public now.

questions.question: Which account from the search results should you select?
questions.why: The search dropdown displays multiple similar usernames like '[account]' and '[account]', requiring you to identify the exact target.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the certainty that the agent is verifying the privacy settings against the correct user profile instead of a similarly named account.
questions.check: Do the search results show more than one username close to the target, and which one matches the handle exactly?
questions.say_example: The search shows <two> names that look almost the same. I'm checking <the exact handle>, the one that's yours.

questions.question: Are you 17 or older, as this download asks you to confirm?
questions.why: The screen displays a warning that Yubo contains age-restricted material and requires confirmation of your age before downloading.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to block the download of age-restricted content to your device.
questions.check: Does the page show an age-confirmation prompt stating the app has age-restricted material?
questions.say_example: It asks to confirm you're 17 or older before downloading <the app>. Only you can answer that one.

questions.question: Does a plain http address now stay on http instead of being upgraded?
questions.why: Manually editing the URL in the address bar to remove the 's' from HTTPS is necessary to test if the disabled security setting actually permits insecure connections.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the direct visual confirmation of seeing the browser successfully load the insecure HTTP version of the site without forcing a secure redirect.
questions.check: After loading a plain http address, does the address bar show http without an upgrade or warning?
questions.say_example: Tested it. Opened <the site> over plain http and it stayed http, no upgrade, no warning. The change is working.

questions.question: Did the insecure-connection test actually load over HTTP, or did the page come back secure?
questions.why: You manually entered an HTTP URL to test the disabled secure connection, but the resulting page displays a secure lock icon indicating an HTTPS connection.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that their requested security setting change actually took effect.
questions.check: After entering an http address to test, does the address bar show http, or a lock and https?
questions.say_example: The test didn't prove it. I typed http, but the page came back with the lock, on https. The setting may not be doing anything on this site - trying another.

questions.question: Did the install proceed without an approval prompt, showing the restriction is really off?
questions.why: Tapping the install button on the App Store pop-up confirms whether the disabled approval setting actually took effect.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the firsthand confirmation that their child can now download apps without triggering an approval request.
questions.check: Does the install proceed without an 'Ask Permission' or approval prompt appearing?
questions.say_example: The download started with no ask-permission prompt. The approval requirement is really off.

questions.question: Are the restricted apps hidden from your App Library search?
questions.why: Seeing no results for the restricted app in the App Library confirms the new privacy setting actually took effect across the device.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the personal peace of mind of seeing firsthand that the restricted app is truly inaccessible on your device.
questions.check: Does an App Library search for the restricted app return no results?
questions.say_example: Searched the App Library for <the app>. Nothing comes up. The restriction is holding.
